h.strategy: Borrow interaction patterns from other empirical sciences: epistasis in genetics (the effect of one mutation depends on genetic background, and beneficial mutations help fitter backgrounds less), diminishing returns in economics, and redundancy in engineered systems. Translate each pattern into a concrete conditional hypothesis about how an edit's effect varies with the parent configuration. Favor predictions that a practitioner thinking only mechanistically would get wrong, especially background-dependent sign changes and weaker gains in already-strong parents. Use conditions that many parents satisfy. In the flaw step, discard analogies that do not transfer and keep only those with a plausible general reason to hold.

hyps.why: A skip on the direct edge already provides a strong residual path, so the conv upgrade on edge 5 shows diminishing returns.
Two conv3x3 inputs into node 3 are partly redundant under sum-aggregation, so the second adds less.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 is fed only via the longer path through node 1, so a conv on edge 5 carries less useful signal.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no input, so edge 4 is dead and upgrading it has no effect.
With edge 5 removed, node 2's output cannot reach node 3, so upgrading edge 2 has little effect.
Adding a skip where there was none creates a new gradient path, which helps more than swapping an existing op.
A strong conv background already gives node 3 a good input, so the extra skip adds less.
Downgrading from conv3x3 loses capacity, so it hurts more than replacing weaker incumbents.
With edge 2 removed, edge 1 is the sole input to node 2, so its quality matters more.
With edge 4 removed, node 3 relies more on edge 5, so upgrading it matters more.
